fixes.explanation: Towns it is, friend. Solomon, Israel's king, gave twenty towns in the land of Galilee to Hiram king of Tyre, who had supplied him with cedar and cypress logs and gold. Most folks hand over a gift card. Solomon handed over a whole map.

That's right. Hiram king of Tyre went out to inspect the towns, and the text says he was not pleased with them. His own words are, “What are these towns you have given me, my brother?” Twenty towns, and he still wasn't pleased.

That's the reason the text gives. Solomon did not consign any of the Israelites to slavery, because they were his men of war, his servants, his officers, his captains, and the commanders of his chariots and cavalry. That's a whole leadership roster.
True, baker. The Israelites were also the chief officers over Solomon's projects, with 550 supervisors over the people who did the work. That's a lot of clipboards.

Not this time, friend. The statement is true. The text says the Israelites were also the chief officers over Solomon's projects, 550 supervisors over the people who did the work. Five hundred fifty supervisors. I'd hate to see that group chat.

Twelve times a year would be far more often than the text says, friend. It says three times a year Solomon offered burnt offerings and peace offerings on the altar he had built for the LORD. Then it says he completed the temple.

Right, baker. Hiram king of Tyre sent his servants, sailors who knew the sea, to serve in the fleet with Solomon's servants. Remember, he's the man who supplied the cedar, cypress and gold. That's a king who sends help when a fleet needs sailors.

Ophir is the place. Hiram's sailors and Solomon's servants sailed there and imported gold, 420 talents of it, and delivered it to Solomon. Sailing for gold makes me feel small, since I once walked across the counter for a sprinkle and thought I'd done something big.
Cyprus is a real island, but it isn't named here. The text says the fleet sailed to Ophir and imported gold from there, 420 talents, and delivered it to Solomon. Ophir is the place the verse names.
